headline: Accessing the Basalt Cliffs of the Yukon River
reservation: Miles Canyon is a public scenic area and does not currently require a permit or entry fee for day use. For those planning to use nearby Schwatka Lake for commercial activities or camping at nearby private sites, separate arrangements must be made with the respective operators.

days.title: Canyon Rims and Suspension Bridges
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Whitehorse City Centre

stops.name: Robert Lowe Suspension Bridge
stops.detail: Cross the Yukon River to view the dramatic basalt walls formed by ancient volcanic activity.

stops.name: Yukon River Loop
stops.detail: Follow the trail south toward Canyon City to see the remains of the tramway used during the Klondike Gold Rush.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes for the short drive from downtown; trail time is approximately 2 hours.
days.note: The suspension bridge can be swaying; use caution during high wind conditions.

days.title: River History and Reservoir Views

stops.name: Schwatka Lake Overlook
stops.detail: Observe the floatplanes taking off from the river above the hydro dam, which changed the canyon's water levels.

stops.name: S.S. Klondike National Historic Site
stops.detail: Visit this nearby sternwheeler to connect the river geography of the canyon with the history of Yukon transportation.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for local transit; sites are within a 10km radius of the canyon.
days.note: Check the local city trail map as some paths may be shared with mountain bikers.

days.title: Basalt Formations and Forest Trails
days.start: Suggested: 9 AM from Miles Canyon Road

stops.name: Upper Canyon Cliffs
stops.detail: Walk the northern ridge for a bird’s-eye view of the turquoise water squeezing through the narrow basalt gap.

stops.name: Chadburn Lake
stops.detail: Extend the day by driving to this nearby emerald lake for a quiet forest walk away from the main river canyon.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for total exploration and local stops; roads are mostly paved but narrow.
days.note: Miles Canyon Road is seasonal and may be closed to vehicles during winter months.

intel.title: Main Canyon Lot
intel.text: The primary parking area is located directly at the suspension bridge trailhead but is small and lacks turning space for large trailers. Secondary parking is available near Schwatka Lake for those walking in.

intel.title: Proximity to Whitehorse
intel.text: Signal strength is generally strong due to the site's proximity to the city. However, deep within the canyon basalt walls, GPS accuracy may fluctuate slightly.

intel.title: City Services
intel.text: Full services are available in Whitehorse, less than 10 minutes away. There are no facilities or fuel stations located at the canyon itself.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Gates
intel.text: The access road to the canyon parking lot is typically gated during the winter season. During this time, the canyon is only accessible via the Millennium Trail on foot or by ski.

intel.title: Terrain Hazards
intel.text: The canyon rim trails are not fenced in most sections and feature steep drops. Stay on marked paths to avoid eroding the fragile volcanic soil.

plan.arrival: Rent a car at YXY airport; the canyon is a very short 10-minute drive south, making it an ideal first stop after checking into a Whitehorse hotel.
plan.vehicle: Standard cars are sufficient for the paved access roads; large RVs should use the Schwatka Lake day-use area instead of the narrow canyon lot.
plan.goldenHour: The east bank of the Yukon River overlooking the basalt cliffs during the long summer twilight.
